Panel of Judges has dismissed the Justice Department's bid to stop California from
processing 20,000 registered voter's ballots in the upcoming midterm election.
NPR's Stu Joffe-Bloch reports a next step in the case as a hearing before a federal
district judge Tuesday.
The DOJ says some 20,000 people on California's voter rolls are likely non-citizens,
though has not provided detailed evidence.
California officials say the DOJ's list is unreliable,
and it's unlawful and infeasible to set aside the ballots this close to election day.
In a two-to-one decision, a Ninth Circuit panel dismissed the DOJ's appeal Monday,
finding the case was not ready for appeal since the district court judge has not yet ruled.
The two judges also made clear they disagreed with DOJ's demands.
Now the case goes back to the district court.
Stu Joffe-Bloch, NPR News.
Heavy rains in the Southwest gave a big boost to Colorado river flows in the Grand Canyon.
Alex Hager of member station KJCZ reports on the welcome change in a historically dry year.
Wildlife and sandy beaches inside the Grand Canyon depend on big brushes of water every
once in a while, but drought and climate change mean lately there isn't much to send downstream
from Lake Powell.
Jen Pells with the nonprofit Grand Canyon Trust says recent rains caused the highest
flows in at least a couple years.
Having the opportunity to have those high flows in the canyon is really important from an
ecological sense.
It will provide benefits.
River watchers originally thought the flows may have been even higher than they were.
Deadly flash floods earlier this summer dammed up a section of the river,
causing the past week's rains to pool around a remote measuring station and give misleading
data.
For NPR News, I'm Alex Hager in Phoenix.

Authorities are looking for a convicted murderer who escaped from a prison in northwest Tennessee.
Officials say 28-year-old Jacob Morley was discovered missing late Sunday at the
